GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node identical to BowlbugEgg.cs:56-63: a single MoveState BITE_MOVE whose FollowUpState is itself, which is also the initial state. No branch node on either side. Executed (monster_probes_b04.py graphs).

guards.what: BITE damage and the block that follows it
guards.rationale: Non-ascension, BowlbugEgg.cs:23-25: BiteDamage 7, ProtectBlock 7. BiteMove (:65-72) awaits the attack and THEN CreatureCmd.GainBlock(Creature, 7, ValueProp.Move) -- the block arrives after the hit, so it cannot absorb the player's Thorns on that same swing. Sim _bite (bowlbugs.py:84-87) is the same order with BlockCmd.apply, and _EGG_BITE_DMG / _EGG_BLOCK = 7 / 7 (bowlbugs.py:25-26). The C# intent is SingleAttackIntent + DefendIntent; the sim's is ATTACK with also=(DEFEND,).

guards.what: no RandomBranchState -- AddBranch bug class not applicable
guards.rationale: Executed (monster_probes_b04.py branches): bowlbug_egg builds no branch node of any kind on either side. Checked against the AddBranch overload table (monster_state_machine step 13): no overload takes a weight as an int, so a positional transliteration can convert a repeat limit into a weight (seam G1's bug class).
